items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : FunLike F R ℝ] (v : F) {c : ℝ} (p : Polynomial R),
  0 ≤ c → ∀ [NonnegHomClass F R ℝ], 0 ≤ Polynomial.gaussNorm v c p
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ R $, if $ c \geq 0 $ and $ v $ is a non-negative valuation (i.e., $ v(a) \geq 0 $ for all $ a \in R $), then the Gauss norm $ \|p\|_v^c $ satisfies $ 0 \leq \|p\|_v^c $. The Gauss norm is defined as the supremum of $ v(a_i) \cdot c^i $ over all coefficients $ a_i $ of $ p $, with $ \|p\|_v^c = 0 $ when $ p $ is the zero polynomial.

items.informal_name: Non-Negativity of Sum of Squares of Integer Polynomials
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (x : α → ℕ) (l : List (Poly α)), 0 ≤ (Poly.sumsq l) x
items.informal_description: For any assignment $x : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ of natural numbers to variables indexed by $\alpha$, the evaluation of the sum of squares of a list of integer polynomials at $x$ yields a non-negative integer, i.e., $\text{sumsq}(l)(x) \geq 0$ for all lists $l$ of polynomials in $\text{Poly}\, \alpha$.

items.informal_name: Absolute Value of Integer Polynomial is Diophantine
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u} (p : Poly α), Dioph.DiophFn fun v => (p v).natAbs
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ with integer coefficients in variables indexed by $ \alpha $, the function that maps each valuation $ v : \alpha \to \mathbb{N} $ to the absolute value of $ p(v) $ is a Diophantine function. This means there exists a polynomial equation in variables indexed by $ \alpha \oplus \beta $ with integer coefficients such that for any $ v : \alpha \to \mathbb{N} $, there exists $ t : \beta \to \mathbb{N} $ making the equation hold if and only if $ |p(v)| $ equals the extended valuation at $ \text{none} $.

items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : SeminormedRing R] (p : Polynomial R) (n : ℕ), 0 ≤ spectralValueTerms p n
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a seminormed ring $ R $ and any natural number $ n $, the $ n $-th term of the spectral value terms sequence is non-negative. Specifically, each term is defined as $ \|p_n\|^{1/(d - n)} $ for $ n < d $ (where $ d $ is the degree of $ p $) and $ 0 $ otherwise, and all such terms satisfy $ \geq 0 $.

items.informal_name: Positivity evaluation for absolute value expressions
items.informal_description: A function that evaluates the strictness level of an absolute value expression by checking if it is of the form $\text{abv}(a)$, verifying the function is a variable, and using the nonnegativity of absolute values to return a strictness level indicating nonnegativity.
The Mahler measure of any polynomial $ p $ is non-negative, i.e., $ \text{MahlerMeasure}(p) \geq 0 $.
